business.sales_model: Mostly direct to global inverter manufacturers, US utilities and end customers; customized engineered-to-order products.
business.new_asset_purpose: Ultra-high-voltage transformer production facility and expansion of existing product lines

governance.audit: Samjong KPMG; FY2025 and H1 2026 clean/unqualified disclosure with no going-concern emphasis; FY2025 ICFR audit unqualified.
governance.alborz_issue: Payment blocked by US Iran sanctions; controlling shareholder had paid on behalf of company; payable recognized and repayment method under discussion.

industry.us_grid_demand: DOE says additional transmission is pressing because of data centers, manufacturing and load growth; Reuters/EIA forecast record US electricity use in 2026-2027.

estimates.note: Current share count adjusts H1 issued shares for the publicly reported 27,000-share July option exercise; valuation impact versus H1 share count is immaterial.

inferences: The primary economic moat is customer qualification, reliability/quality reputation, custom engineering and direct relationships in a supply-constrained market, not patent-like technology exclusivity.
H1 customer concentration is the largest structural risk: the top four disclosed customers represent about 89.5% of H1 sales, materially above FY2025 top-five concentration of about 61.0%.

The KRW69.25B land/building acquisition is financially survivable from existing liquidity, but ultra-high-voltage expansion is a meaningful capital-allocation test because it moves SANIL beyond its historical 72.5kV niche.

Current 36-37% operating margins may contain both structural mix/scale benefits and temporary scarcity pricing; underwriting should assume some mean reversion rather than extrapolate peak margins indefinitely.
